3. Defendant No. I contested the suit by filing written statements and contended inter alia that, the suit was barred by limitation and bad for defect of parties and also stated that, the proforma defendant Nos. 13 and 14 never executed any Bainapatra or delivered possession of the suit land, that Suresh had no son in the name of Sankar (Proforma opposite party No. 14), but died leaving behind two sons namely Subrata and Shuhendu; that Ratish Chowdhury proforma defendant No. 13 sold Dag No. 2569 of the 2nd schedule comprising an area of 2.16 acres to this defendant by, registered kabala dated 03.06.1972 and delivered possession thereof and since then this defendant was possessing the same. The further case of the defendant petitioner was that Subrata and Shubendu sons of Suresh Chowdhury contracted to sell Dag No. 2283 of the 2nd schedule land with defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on 10.04.1964 and delivered possession thereof. That the defendant took settlement in 1358 B.S. of the suit 3rd scheduled land from the zamindar Romesh Chandra Chowdhury and Suresh Chandra Chowdhury and since then was possessing the same as residence and living there with their family. That as the record of right wrongly prepared in the name of Ex-land Lord, this defendant filed Title Suit No. 150 of 1969 in the first court of Munsif Sylhet for correction of the record of rights; that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 202 of 19769 was not binding upon this defendant as he was not a party to the suit and that the plaintiff had no right title or interest over the suit land and hence prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 6. Mr. Kazi Mozzammelul Huq with, Mr. M.A. Gaffer, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that both the courts below committed serious error of law in passing their judgments and decrees in not appreciating the settled principle of law that the plaintiff was to succeed on the basis of his own evidence and not on the witnesses of the other side if any., He further, submitted that both the Courts on misreading and non-reading the oral and documentary evidence disbelieved the case of the defendant No. 1. He further argued that both the courts below failed to appreciate the proof of defendants title by of pattan, kabala, Bainapatra and all the evidence on his side proved the said facts and also the possession of defendant No.1. Both the courts below misdirected themselves in holding a ground that the plaintiff failed to state specifying the suit land and further the failed to appreciate the provision as laid town in section 30 of State Acquisition of Tenancy Act of 1950. He finally argued that the plain-tiffs opposite party completely failed to prove possession followed by dispossession by any sufficient oral and documentary evidence. In support of his contention he referred the case of Imanuddin Barbi vs. Lilabati Das, reported in 32 DLR-75, Sultan Ahmed vs. Md. Waziullah and others, reported in 7 BLD-235, Munshi Dudhu in and others vs. Rahimuddin and others, reported in 16 DLR 56, Barada Prasanna Lod and others, vs. Kobbad Mia, reported in 13 DLR-765, The Crown vs. Mongal Khan, reported in 6 DLR-490. 

 7. Mr. M. A. Samid with, Mr. M.G.H. Ruhullah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties submitted that both the courts below acted legally and com-mitted no mistake in passing their judgments and decrees. He further argued that the trial court rightly observed that Suresh had only one son which was evident from the fact that the defendant in Title Suit No. 150 of 1969 for correction of record of right made Subrata Chowdhury son of late Suresh Chowdhury as defendant No. 2 and none else and this clearly showed that Suresh had only one son and it also got strength from the certified copy of the petition filed by defendant in Title Execution Case No. 5 of 1970. In the said petition Sunkar was admitted by the defendant as only son of Suresh and from this evidence it was clear that Suresh had only one son namely Sankar and not Subrata. He also submitted that the lower appellate court had rightly observed that Ext.-C হইতেছে দেওয়ানী ১৫০/১৯৬৯ নং মোকদ্দমার ডিক্রীর সই মুহুরী নকল। উক্ত দেওয়ানী ১৫০/১৯৬৯ নং মোকদ্দমাটি বাদী ইন্তাজ আলী দায়ের করেন রেকর্ড সংশোধনের মোকদ্দমা এবং উক্ত মোকদ্দমার ২নং বিবাদী হিসাবে সুব্রত চন্দ্র চৌধুরী পিল মৃত সুরেশ চন্দ্র চৌধুরীকে একমাত্র ছেলে হিসাবে দেখানো হয়েছে। পি.ডব্লিউ-১ অঞ্জন খা তাহার জবান বন্দীতে বলেন ১৪নং বিবাদী শংকর প্রসাদ চৌধুরী সুরেশ চন্দ্র এর একমাত্র ছেলে। --------   and on this score the lower appellate court had observed that though the defendant No. 1, dismissed the decree of the Title Suit No. 202 of 1969 and also Title Execution No. 5 of 1970 but the defendant did not file any suit challenging the legality of Title Suit No. 202 of 1969 and Title execution Case No. 5 of 1970 and as such the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court in Title Suit No. 202 of 1969 was valid in the eye of law. He finally argued that the petitioner never was in possession of the suit property since he neither mentioned his possession any where in written statement or memo appeal or Revisional application. In support of his argument he referred the cases of Zamir Uddin Ahmed Vs. Ziaul Huq and others, reported in 49 DLR622 and Md. Shah Alam Vs. Musammat Panda Begum, reported in 17BLD(AD)145.
